inputs.original_text: John Lahart, the Fianna Fáil TD for Dublin South-West, is calling for reform of the inheritance tax exemption thresholds, calling the current system ‘wholly unfair’ and discriminatory against those without children. This follows recent contributions from party colleagues on reviewing how the tax applies across different family structures. It exposes the systemic discrimination baked into our institutions, where policies have long favored traditional family models and reinforced historical inequalities that disadvantage vulnerable groups who don't have children. Real institutional reform is needed to dismantle these biases and advance social justice and equality for everyone.
inputs.modified_text: John Lahart, the Fianna Fáil TD for Dublin South-West, is pushing to reform inheritance tax exemption thresholds and calling the current system ‘wholly unfair’ and discriminatory against those without children. This lines up with similar noises from his party colleagues about rethinking the rules for different family structures. What this really shows is the relentless pressure from progressive activists to strip away long-standing protections for traditional families. These policies were never meant to be some kind of bias; they reflect basic common sense about passing on the fruits of hard work and responsibility to the next generation within stable family units. Instead of strengthening what works to preserve cultural continuity and social order, the push now is to treat child-rearing as optional and force equal treatment for those who opt out. We don't need more so-called institutional reform to advance social justice; we need to defend the family as the foundation of a healthy nation rather than erode it under slogans that prioritize individualism over duty.
